To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose two simultaneous shield insertion/net ordering (SINO/NF and SINO/NB) problems to minimize capacitive and inductivene noise; we propose effective algorithms to solve the two problems; we show that our algorithms use fewer shields compared to state-of-the-art algorithms and the lower bound of optimal solutions; we show the high fidelity of Keff model in predicting noise.

(1) simultaneous shield insertion and noise-free net ordering is needed to minimize both capacitative and inductive noise and (2) the Keff model is an effective and efficient figure of merit for the inductive noise.

(i) existing net ordering formulations are insufficient for the simultaneous shield insertion and inductive coupling noise minimization, (ii) shield insertion is essential for inductive noise minimization, and (iii) the proposed Keff model has high fidelity versus the actual noise voltage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic layout optimization to minimize the noise of multiple nets, where the noise is modeled by capacitive and inductance coupling.
the following questions: (1) What is the best way to insert shields for a set of nets?
two important problems: (1) how to automatically insert shields and order nets for capacitive and/or inductive noise minimization, and (2) how to model inductive noise in an efficient way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we present the first study that considers both capacitive and magnetic noise, and we present the first algorithm that simultaneously optimizes shield insertion and net order to minimize both capacive and magnetic noise.
we propose the first SINO formulation and algorithm to minimize both capaci tive and inductive noise simultaneously.

our SINO approach is able to significantly reduce both capacitive and/or inductive noise in an integrated circuit layout, and is able to provide a high-quality layout solution in terms of area and noise reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the simultaneous shield insertion and noise-aware net ordering (SINONE) algorithm is the most efficient and effective solution to the capacitive and in-ductive noise-aware shielded layout optimization problem.
we have formulated the SINO problem and proposed effective approximate algorithms to find SINO solutions that are free of capacitive or under a given inductive noise.

the proposed SINO algorithms are able to find the minimal area shield insertion and net-ordering solution that is free from capacitive and inductice noise, and the SINO/NF algorithm provides a theoretical upper bound of the area for the optimal SINO solutions, while the SINO/NBF algorithm provides a practical upper bound of the SINO/NFB solutions under the practical noise bound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shield insertion and net order optimization can be done simultaneously to minimize capacitive and inductively coupled noise.
shield insertion and net reordering should be performed simultaneously to minimize both capacitative and inductive noise.
simultaneous shield insertion and optimal net ordering can significantly reduce both capacitive and magnetic noise.
